QF.id: Securities Types Features and Asset Allocation Concepts_45

question.text: During a period of high inflation, an investor notices that the real value of their fixed deposit returns is being eroded. Which additional asset class should they consider adding to their portfolio to hedge against inflation?

answer.text: Commodities such as gold, as commodity prices tend to rise during inflationary periods
More bank fixed deposits at the same interest rate
Long-duration government bonds with fixed coupons
Savings bank deposits for better liquidity

explanation.text: The Logic: Commodity prices are usually higher during periods of rising inflation, so commodity exposure can act as a hedge against inflation. Fixed-income assets, by contrast, can be adversely affected when inflation rises. The Trap: More FDs at the same rate (option B) face the same erosion. Long-duration fixed-coupon bonds (option C) lose value when yields rise alongside inflation. Savings deposits (option D) typically earn even lower returns than FDs. Note: The source-supported point is that commodities can hedge inflation while fixed income can be adversely affected — without prescribing a specific allocation percentage.
